questiontext.text:
A ship is at \(P({@lat0@}^\circ\,\mathrm{[[if test="n0"]]N[[else]]S[[/if]]}, {@lon0@}^\circ\,\mathrm{[[if test="e0"]]E[[else]]W[[/if]]})\).

(a) It sails [[if test="is(d1=1)"]]due north[[else]]due south[[/if]] along its meridian through \({@dphi@}^\circ\) of latitude. Give its new latitude.

[[input:ans1]] \(^\circ\) [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Instead, it sails [[if test="is(d2=1)"]]due east[[else]]due west[[/if]] along its parallel through \({@dlam@}^\circ\) of longitude. Give its new longitude.

[[input:ans3]] \(^\circ\) [[input:ans4]] [[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
(a) Count along the meridian, with the equator as \(0^\circ\). [[if test="xeq"]]The first \({@lat0@}^\circ\) take the ship to the equator; the remaining \({@dphi-lat0@}^\circ\) take it into the other hemisphere.[[else]][[if test="away"]]The ship moves away from the equator, so its latitude grows: \({@lat0@}^\circ + {@dphi@}^\circ\).[[else]]The ship moves towards the equator but does not reach it: \({@lat0@}^\circ - {@dphi@}^\circ\).[[/if]][[/if]] New latitude: \({@lat1@}^\circ\,\mathrm{[[if test="n1"]]N[[else]]S[[/if]]}\).

(b) Think of longitude as a number line from \(180^\circ\,\mathrm{W}\) through \(0^\circ\) to \(180^\circ\,\mathrm{E}\), joined up at \(180^\circ\). [[if test="x180"]]The ship passes the \(180^\circ\) meridian: counting on gives \({@unred@}^\circ\), which is \(360^\circ - {@unred@}^\circ = {@lon1@}^\circ\) on the other side.[[else]][[if test="xgr"]]The ship crosses the Greenwich meridian, so the letter changes.[[else]]The ship stays on the same side of Greenwich.[[/if]][[/if]] New longitude: \({@lon1@}^\circ\,\mathrm{[[if test="e1"]]E[[else]]W[[/if]]}\).

questiondescription.text:
Navigation: new position after moving

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.7 (b) / Essential 2.3 (b): Find the new latitude or longitude of a ship after it sails along a meridian or a parallel, across the equator, Greenwich or the 180 degree meridian.

Core and Essential

This question is original to this project.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core and Essential Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text:
[[if test="xeq"]]

The size is right, but the ship crossed the equator: sailing \({@dphi@}^\circ\) [[if test="is(d1=1)"]]due north[[else]]due south[[/if]] from \({@lat0@}^\circ\,\mathrm{[[if test="n0"]]N[[else]]S[[/if]]}\) takes it \({@lat1@}^\circ\) into the other hemisphere.

[[else]]

The size is right. Check N or S: the ship is still in the [[if test="n1"]]northern[[else]]southern[[/if]] hemisphere.

[[/if]]

[[if test="xeq"]]

You added \({@dphi@}^\circ\) to \({@lat0@}^\circ\). The ship is moving towards the equator, and it reaches the equator after only \({@lat0@}^\circ\). Where does the rest of the move take it?

[[else]][[if test="away"]]

You took the difference between \({@lat0@}^\circ\) and \({@dphi@}^\circ\). The ship moves away from the equator, so its latitude grows.

[[else]]

You added \({@dphi@}^\circ\) to \({@lat0@}^\circ\). The ship moves towards the equator, so its latitude falls.

[[/if]][[/if]]

falsefeedback.text: Your answer is [[if test="is(yd>0)"]]\({@yd@}^\circ\) north of[[else]][[if test="is(yd<0)"]]\({@-yd@}^\circ\) south of[[else]]the same as[[/if]][[/if]] the starting latitude, but the ship sailed \({@dphi@}^\circ\) [[if test="is(d1=1)"]]due north[[else]]due south[[/if]]. Draw the meridian with the equator marked, then count from \({@lat0@}^\circ\,\mathrm{[[if test="n0"]]N[[else]]S[[/if]]}\).

truefeedback.text: Longitude only goes up to \(180^\circ\). Your \({@ans3@}^\circ\) is past the \(180^\circ\) meridian: measure it the shorter way round from Greenwich instead, which is the rest of the full turn of \(360^\circ\), and change the letter.

[[if test="x180"]]

The size is right, but the ship crossed the \(180^\circ\) meridian, so the letter changes.

[[else]][[if test="xgr"]]

The size is right, but the ship crossed the Greenwich meridian, so the letter changes.

[[else]]

The size is right. Check E or W: the ship did not cross the Greenwich or the \(180^\circ\) meridian.

[[/if]][[/if]]

falsefeedback.text: Your answer is [[if test="is(yd>0)"]]\({@yd@}^\circ\) east of[[else]][[if test="is(yd<0)"]]\({@-yd@}^\circ\) west of[[else]]the same as[[/if]][[/if]] the starting longitude, but the ship sailed \({@dlam@}^\circ\) [[if test="is(d2=1)"]]due east[[else]]due west[[/if]]. Moving east increases an east longitude and decreases a west one. Past \(0^\circ\) or \(180^\circ\), the letter changes.
